title: feat: add Antigravity (Windsurf fork) Cascade extraction with reasoni…
body:
## What

  Adds `extract_antigravity.py` — an extractor for Antigravity, Google's
  internal fork of Windsurf used in their Gemini ecosystem.

  ## How it works

  Unlike the other extractors in this repo (which read SQLite or JSONL files),
  Antigravity's conversations are stored as protobuf `.pb` files without a
  bundled schema. The workaround is its local Connect-RPC HTTP API, exposed by
  the running language server process.

  Credit: the technique of querying the language server's Connect-RPC API
  (including the required headers and method names) was originally documented
  in https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar.

  The script:
  1. Auto-discovers the language server PID, CSRF token, and port from `ps aux` + `lsof`
  2. Calls `GetAllCascadeTrajectories` to list conversations
  3. Calls `GetCascadeTrajectorySteps` per conversation to fetch all steps
  4. Maps `CORTEX_STEP_TYPE_USER_INPUT` → user messages
  5. Maps `CORTEX_STEP_TYPE_NOTIFY_USER` → assistant messages
  6. Collects `CORTEX_STEP_TYPE_PLANNER_RESPONSE.thinking` blocks (grouped by
     `executionId`) and attaches them as a `thoughts` field on each assistant
     message — equivalent to what `extract_gemini.py` does for Gemini reasoning

  ## Requirements

  - Antigravity must be running when you run the script (API-based extraction)
  - Python 3.6+, no external dependencies (stdlib only: `ssl`, `subprocess`,
    `urllib`, `re`, `json`, `pathlib`, `platform`)

  ## Output sample

  ```json
  {
    "messages": [
      {"role": "user", "content": "...", "timestamp": "..."},
      {
        "role": "assistant",
        "content": "...",
        "timestamp": "...",
        "model": "MODEL_PLACEHOLDER_M8",
        "thoughts": "**Analyzing the request**\n\nOkay, so..."
      }
    ],
    "source": "antigravity-cascade",
    "cascade_id": "...",
    "summary": "Aircraft Maintenance Audit Script",
    "step_count": 55,
    "created_time": "2025-12-04T19:08:09Z",
    "workspaces": ["/Users/jr/projects/my-app"]
  }

  Changes

  - extract_antigravity.py — new extractor (stdlib only)
  - README.md — added section 9, quick start command, output filename example
  - extract_all.sh — added Antigravity block with appropriate running note

title: Add SQLite database support for OpenCode v1.2.0+

## Summary

This PR adds support for extracting conversations from OpenCode's new SQLite database format (v1.2.0+) while maintaining full backward compatibility with the legacy JSON storage format.

## Changes

- **SQLite Support**: New `extract_from_sqlite()` function to read from `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`
- **Dual Format Support**: Automatically detects and extracts from both SQLite and legacy JSON storage
- **Message Part Types**: Properly handles all message part types including text, tool calls, and reasoning
- **Source Tracking**: Conversations now tracked by source (SQLite v1.2.0+, Legacy JSON <v1.2.0, Desktop)

## Backward Compatibility

- Legacy JSON storage still fully supported for older OpenCode versions
- Falls back to legacy format when SQLite database is not found
- No breaking changes to existing functionality

## Testing

Tested with both SQLite database format and legacy JSON storage from various OpenCode installations.

title: Add cursor-agent CLI extractor
body:
## What

Adds `extract_cursor_cli.py` — extraction for the **`cursor-agent` terminal CLI** history, which the existing `extract_cursor.py` (GUI SQLite `state.vscdb`/`cursorDiskKV`) does not cover.

## The format

Each agent session lives at `~/.cursor/chats/<chatId>/<agentId>/store.db` — a content-addressed SQLite blob store:

- **`blobs`** table: `id` (sha256 hex) → `data`. Message blobs are JSON (`{role, content, id, ...}`); tree nodes are protobuf-framed lists of 32-byte child blob-id refs (frame = `0x0a 0x20` + 32 bytes).
- **`meta`** table: single hex-encoded JSON row with `agentId`, `latestRootBlobId`, `name`, `mode`, `createdAt`.

Ordered messages are reconstructed by DFS-walking blob refs from `latestRootBlobId`.

## Output

Same shape/conventions as the other extractors — `extracted_data/cursor_cli_<ts>.jsonl`, one conversation per line, with `source: "cursor-agent-cli"`, `chat_id`, `agent_id`, `title`, `mode`, `created_at`, and `has_code_context`/`has_diffs` flags. Stdlib only, no new deps.

## Integration

- Wired into `extract_all.sh` (detected via the same `Total conversations: [1-9]` convention).
- Documented in `README.md` (script list + Basic Usage).

## Testing

Runs cleanly on macOS (83 conversations) and Linux (1,273). `bash -n extract_all.sh` and a Python parse check both pass.

title: Add omp (Oh My Pi) extractor
body:
Adds `extract_omp.py`, an extractor for [omp (Oh My Pi)](https://omp.sh) — repo: [can1357/oh-my-pi](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi). It was the one harness in my fleet this toolkit did not cover.

## Storage layout

- Transcripts: `~/.omp/agent/sessions/<slugified-cwd>/<ISO8601>_<uuid>.jsonl` (newline-delimited records, one per line)
- Sidecar tool logs: same path minus `.jsonl`, as a directory
- Prompt history: `~/.omp/agent/history.db` (`history` table)

Discovery honours `$OMP_HOME` / `$OMP_DATA_DIR`, then `~/.omp/agent`, with macOS/Linux/Windows fallbacks, matching the existing scripts' pattern. Accepts either `<dir>/agent/sessions` or `<dir>/sessions`.

## Extracted

- User / assistant / developer messages
- Thinking (reasoning) blocks
- Tool calls with arguments; tool results attached to the owning assistant turn
- Per-turn model attribution, tracked across mid-session model switches
- Compaction and branch-summary boundaries (kept as markers so truncated context is visible rather than silently dropped)
- Project path, session title, sidecar tool-log filenames

Output uses the existing conversation schema (`messages` / `source` / `session_id` / `name` / `project_path`), so it merges cleanly with the other extractors.

## Notes

- Stdlib only, consistent with the rest of the toolkit.
- `history.db` is opened `mode=ro&immutable=1` so a live WAL is never mutated.
- Records of type `custom` are extension-private payloads and are skipped; `custom_message` turns are kept and flagged.
- Session transcripts prefixed `__` (e.g. `__advisor.jsonl`) are extension sidecars and are skipped.
- Wired into `extract_all.sh`; README updated in the script list, usage, output listing, and storage-formats sections.

## Verification

Ran against a real install: 202 transcripts → 200 conversations, 197 with assistant turns, 91,971 messages, 179 with thinking blocks, 171 with tool calls/results, 2,402 prompt-history rows, across 10 projects. Spot-checked a record for intact tool-call arguments and tool-result bodies. `bash -n extract_all.sh` and `python3 -m py_compile extract_omp.py` both clean.

title: Enterprise-safe harness export for Claude Code (portable learnings + redaction + audit)
body:
## Enterprise-safe harness export for Claude Code

Adds a way to carry out your **portable learnings and settings** (CLAUDE.md, memory, skills, slash commands, agents, settings, and your personal prompt patterns) when leaving an enterprise or sensitive-data environment - **without** carrying out proprietary code, secrets, or internal paths.

The existing extractors dump raw conversations (the README warns the output "may include proprietary code, API keys/secrets, personal file paths"), which is a non-starter in a sensitive setting. This PR adds a redaction + audit layer, scoped to Claude Code.

### What's new
- **`sanitize.py`** - local, offline, stdlib-only redaction: known secret shapes (AWS, GitHub, Anthropic/OpenAI, Google, Slack, Stripe, GitLab, npm, DigitalOcean, SendGrid, Twilio, PEM and PGP key blocks), `key = value` assignments whose key names a credential, `Authorization`-style headers, credentials in URL userinfo and query strings, credential-bearing CLI flags including the split argv form, XML element values, emails, IPv4 and IPv6, and home paths including UNC and `~user` forms. Key names are sanitized as well as values. A high-entropy backstop flags leftovers per file.
- **`export_claude_harness.py`** - discovers `~/.claude` installs and runs three toggleable collectors into a bundle + `MANIFEST.json`:
  - **config** (CLAUDE.md, settings, MCP, skills, commands, agents, memory)
  - **prompts** (your user-authored prompts only, with the events Claude Code injects into the user turn excluded)
  - **conversations** (opt-in; `strict` default *drops* code/diffs/tool output, `balanced` keeps-but-sanitizes)
- 174 tests, including a CLI-level end-to-end check that plants a canary in every documented asset and searches the whole bundle, `MANIFEST.json` and file names included.

### Guarantees
- **No leakage by default** - strict mode (default) drops tool calls, tool results, diffs, and any content shape it cannot positively identify as text, structurally rather than by regex.
- **Selective extraction** - conversations are opt-in; default `--include config,prompts`.
- **Auditability** - `MANIFEST.json` records per-file sha256/bytes, redaction counts, what was dropped, and warnings; `--dry-run` writes *only* the manifest so it can be reviewed before anything is materialized.

### Usage
```bash
python3 export_claude_harness.py                                   # safe defaults: config + prompts, strict
python3 export_claude_harness.py --dry-run                         # review what would be exported
python3 export_claude_harness.py --include config,prompts,conversations
python3 export_claude_harness.py --include config,prompts,conversations --redact-level balanced
```

### Notes
- Python 3 standard library only; no new dependencies; no network calls. `detect-secrets` is used only if already installed.
- Redaction is default-safe and reviewable, not a claim of provable purity for arbitrary code. It does not cover file and directory names, bare usernames outside a path, or low-entropy passwords that appear without a key name or a cue word. The README has the current list and the review procedure; `MANIFEST.json` warnings are the backstop.
- Only these extensions are exported from the config trees: `.md .txt .json .yaml .yml .toml .sh .py`. Anything else is left out and named in the manifest warnings.
- This branch went through an independent security audit after it was opened, then four further rounds against the fixes. 125 defects found and closed, each with a regression test; see the last two commits.
- There is no CI on this repo, so the suite has only run locally: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`.
- Existing extractors are untouched.

title: Add support for Grok Build
body:
## Feature request

Please add extraction support for [Grok Build](https://github.com/xai-org/grok-build), xAI's terminal coding agent.

Grok Build persists complete sessions locally, so it looks like a good fit for this project. By default, sessions live under:

```text
~/.grok/sessions/<encoded-cwd>/<session-id>/
```

`GROK_HOME` can override the base directory.

According to Grok Build's session documentation, each session can contain files such as:

```text
summary.json
updates.jsonl
chat_history.jsonl
plan.json
rewind_points.jsonl
signals.json
feedback.jsonl
subagents/
```

The most useful sources appear to be `updates.jsonl` for the ACP session update stream and `chat_history.jsonl` for raw model messages.

It would be useful to have an `extract_grok.py` extractor, wired into `extract_all.sh`, that follows the same normalized JSONL output used by the existing extractors and preserves as much as possible of:

- user prompts and assistant responses
- tool calls and tool results
- timestamps
- working directory / project path
- model information
- session ID, title, and summary metadata
- token / turn usage
- parent and subagent session relationships
- file/edit context where it can be reconstructed from the session events

Official session format documentation:
https://github.com/xai-org/grok-build/blob/main/crates/codegen/xai-grok-pager/docs/user-guide/17-sessions.md

Because the storage is already plain JSON/JSONL and documented upstream, this may be simpler and more robust than some of the SQLite-based integrations already supported here.

title: Add Grok Build (grok CLI) session extractor
body:
Closes #22

Adds extraction support for [Grok Build](https://github.com/xai-org/grok-build), xAI's terminal coding agent, following the [documented session format](https://github.com/xai-org/grok-build/blob/main/crates/codegen/xai-grok-pager/docs/user-guide/17-sessions.md).

## What's included

### `extract_grok.py` (new)

- **Discovery**: checks `$GROK_HOME` and `~/.grok` for a `sessions/` tree; walks exactly the two documented levels (`sessions/<urlencoded-cwd>/<session-id>/`), skipping stray files like the root `session_search.sqlite` index, project-level `prompt_history.jsonl`, and images-only session stubs.
- **Conversation**: reads `chat_history.jsonl` (the raw model log) as the source of truth:
  - `user` records -> user messages (flattens content-block arrays; skips the injected `<user_info>` environment preamble)
  - `assistant` records -> assistant messages with `model` and normalized `tool_calls` (the JSON-in-a-string `function.arguments` are parsed)
  - `reasoning` records -> attached as `reasoning` on the following assistant message
  - `tool_result` records -> attached as `tool_results` to the assistant message that issued the call
- **Merged from `updates.jsonl`** (the ACP display log, which carries what the chat log lacks): per-message timestamps (`params._meta.agentTimestampMs`, with a unix-seconds fallback), tool result timestamps, and tool failure status (`is_error`).
- **Metadata from `summary.json`**: session ID, cwd, generated title/summary, created/updated timestamps, model, `head_branch`, `parent_session_id`, and `agent_name`. When `summary.json` is missing, the project path is recovered from the URL-encoded group directory name (honoring the `.cwd` slug-override file for long paths) and the model is backfilled from message-level model IDs.
- **Token/turn usage** from `signals.json` (emitted as `usage`).
- **Subagent relationships**: per-subagent `meta.json` entries from the session's `subagents/` directory (emitted as `subagents`).
- Output follows the same normalized JSONL shape as the other extractors (`source: "grok-build"`), written to `extracted_data/grok_conversations_<timestamp>.jsonl`. Stdlib only, matching the rest of the toolkit.

### Wiring

- `extract_all.sh`: new Grok Build block (same tee/grep pattern as the other tools).
- `README.md`: script section, quick-start command, output listing, and a storage-format note.

## Verification

Verified against a synthetic `$GROK_HOME` fixture built from the documented format: a full session (summary, signals, chat history with system/user_info/user/reasoning/assistant/tool_result records, ACP updates with prompt indexes and a failed tool status, and a subagent `meta.json`) plus a `.cwd`-override group and decoy files. The extractor produced the expected normalized output: preamble and stubs skipped, reasoning and tool results attached to the right messages, timestamps and `is_error` merged from the display log, and all metadata fields populated. Also verified `bash -n extract_all.sh` and the no-installation path.

title: fix: preserve special characters in Cursor database paths
body:
Cursor GUI and CLI extraction can lose conversations when a database's directory contains `#`, `?`, or a literal percent escape. The raw filesystem path is interpolated into a SQLite URI, so those characters are treated as URI syntax. GUI extractors return empty results; the CLI can fail while reading the wrong database.

Construct the file URI with `Path(...).resolve().as_uri()` before appending `mode=ro` at all five Cursor connection sites. Update the README's read-only example accordingly.

The regression creates synthetic SQLite databases for all five supported extraction paths and verifies message recovery plus unchanged database bytes for plain and special-character paths (20 combinations). The original implementation fails all 15 special-character combinations; after the change all 12 repository tests pass with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`. `git diff --check` passes. Tests do not discover or read any real assistant history.

Prepared with AI assistance and verified locally.

title: Add pi and omp extractors; fix Cursor full-table scan
body:
## Summary
- `extract_pi.py`: extracts pi coding-agent sessions from `~/.pi/agent/sessions/**.jsonl`. It follows the `parentId` tree back from the last entry, so it exports the active branch. Output is OpenAI-shaped messages: `reasoning` from thinking blocks, `tool_calls`, and `role: "tool"` results carrying `tool_call_id`/`name`/`is_error`. Each message keeps its `model`/`provider`/`usage`/timestamps. Each session keeps its `system_prompt`, `tools` and `model_changes`, and compaction summaries are included.
- `extract_omp.py`: the same format for omp (oh-my-pi) under `~/.omp/agent/sessions`. Advisor and subagent sessions are flagged `subagent: true`.
- `extract_cursor.py`: the bubble lookup used a parameterized `LIKE`, which cannot use the key index, so it ran a full table scan for every composer. On a 9.3 GB `state.vscdb` the extractor ran for more than 20 minutes without finishing. A key-range query now finishes in about a minute.
- Adds a README section, `extract_all.sh` entries and `tests/test_extract_pi.py`.

## Testing
- `python3 -m pytest tests`: 14 passed. `ruff check` on the new files: clean.
- Ran on a real machine: 1,174 omp and 1,386 pi sessions extracted. The extracted message counts are within about 2% of the raw entry counts; the difference is abandoned branches.

title: Add extract_devin.py — Devin Desktop (Windsurf successor) ACP sessions
body:
## Summary
- New `extract_devin.py` covering **Devin Desktop** (the successor to Windsurf). Its conversation store is not covered by `extract_windsurf.py`: one SQLite DB per session at `<Devin>/User/acp-messages/<uuid>.db` (`meta` + `messages(position, kind, payload JSON)`), with session names registered in `User/globalStorage/state.vscdb` under `windsurf.acp.messageStore.session.*` keys.

title: feat: add ZCode SQLite conversation extraction
body:
ZCode conversations are not covered by the existing extractors. This adds `extract_zcode.py` for the SQLite store at `~/.zcode/cli/db/db.sqlite`, with an optional `--db` path.

The extractor preserves message text, reasoning, tool calls and results, attachment metadata, and session metadata. It also exports parent session IDs, task types, goals, and todos. It opens the source read-only and exports a temporary SQLite backup, including committed WAL rows. Temporary database files are removed on success and failure.

The change adds the extractor to `extract_all.sh`, documents its use, and includes 12 offline regression tests with synthetic fixtures. The ZCode extractor requires Python 3.7 or later.

## Validation

- `python -m unittest discover -s tests`: all 34 tests passed locally with Python 3.13.15.
- `bash -n extract_all.sh` and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Python 3.7 syntax parsing: passed. Python 3.7 runtime execution was not tested.
- Tested locally on my machine against a real ZCode database: 327 conversations and 15,352 messages exported successfully. A local verifier compared exported text, reasoning, tool data, attachments, and selected metadata against the database and found no differences.
- The real-data export contained 16,600 tool calls and 16,598 results. The two remaining calls were still marked `running` in the source.
- The source database and its WAL/SHM files had identical hashes before and after the test. Conversation contents were checked only by local code and were not included in logs, fixtures, or this PR. Temporary real-data copies and exports were deleted after validation.

## Compatibility and scope

This has been tested against one local ZCode database. Future ZCode updates may change storage paths, tables, fields, or part formats. I do not guarantee that this extractor will remain compatible with future ZCode releases.

The extractor keeps sessions separate and preserves parent IDs. It does not reconstruct ancestor messages or read legacy JSON stores. It skips `step-start`, `step-finish`, `timeline`, and `compaction` parts. Live WAL coverage uses a synthetic database with an open writer and committed WAL rows. Continuous concurrent-write stress testing was not performed.
